pr_title: Fix getaddrinfo() to respect socket type hints
pr_body:
If getaddrinfo() was called with AI_PASSIVE flag in hints,
returned address defaulted to SOCK_STREAM and IPPROTO_TCP.
Fixed so that SOCK_DGRAM leads to correct address type
that can be fed to bind() directly.

Same hard coding was visible when numerical IPv4 address string
was converted to binary. That is also fixed to respect hints now.

Fixes #30686

Signed-off-by: Seppo Takalo <seppo.takalo@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: Thanks for looking into this. getaddrinfo() implementation is known to be incomplete (doesn't support all flags/features). Did you consider extending tests/net/socket/getaddrinfo for this case, to make sure it won't regress again in the future?

The `getaddrinfo_null_host()` defaulted to IPv4.
Now that I added handling of the `hints` parameter, I was not sure which one should I default with address type `AF_UNSPEC`. I'm now returning IPv4 address, but modern Unix/POSIX machines return IPv6 because they may still `bind()` and be able to serve IPv4 clients. But how does the IP stack in Zephyr behave when listening with IPv6 any-address?

> But how does the IP stack in Zephyr behave when listening with IPv6 any-address?

Defaulting to IPv4 is probably ok now. I think we do not return IPv4 address when listening IPv6 one.

> but modern Unix/POSIX machines return IPv6

And that causes various trouble to the innocent users. I don't have references handy, but I read about that more than once, and faced that myself too. I actually believe the pendulum swung in the opposite direction by now, and various Linux distros let the IPv6 committee do its job (promoting IPv6) and themselves doing their job (serving, not confusing, their users, and that means IPv4-by-default).

> But how does the IP stack in Zephyr behave when listening with IPv6 any-address?

We don't have that Linux feature implemented. (And I'm talking about Linux, because that's what we use as an affinity for (many) things POSIX leaves underspecified. If you have references where POSIX prescribes a particular behavior in that regard, please share them.) So, to listen to both IPv4 and IPv6, a Zephyr application needs to have 2 listening sockets (and how various samples we have in samples/net/sockets/ do).

issue_context.title: getaddrinfo() does not respect socket type
comments: Indeed, the code seems to hard code `SOCK_STREAM` type in this case. See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/905f496603b905a05d8ae41d81b2cac7987232e7/subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c#L129 for details. The fix looks quite simple, @SeppoTakalo would you be able to fix this and submit a PR?

review_comments: Tests look ok, but please put them in the separate commit. So one commit for the actual fix, and the other commit for tests.

Sure.
Separated to two commits now.
